title: CHAPTER 12: RECENT LEGAL DEVELOPMENTS AND LANDMARK CASES

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Covers the major provisions and structural changes brought by the New Criminal Laws (2023).
Analyzes essential Supreme Court precedents impacting Banking Law and financial regulation.
Examines landmark Constitutional Cases and their impact on fundamental rights and governance.
Summarizes recent legal updates critical for competitive law and general studies examinations.

cells: 358 sections (vs 511); organised crime as specific offence; terrorism separate chapter; community service as punishment; sedition removed (treason redefined); petty organised crime added
531 sections; mandatory audio-video recording of crime scene; forensic investigation mandatory for offences >7 years; timeline for trial; undertrial relief; Zero FIR; e-FIR
170 sections; electronic records primary evidence; video conferencing for evidence; electronic signatures; joint trials; secondary evidence provisions updated

blocks.content: RECENT LEGAL DEVELOPMENTS AND LANDMARK CASES
12.2 Landmark Supreme Court Cases in Banking Law

cells: Upheld constitutionality of SARFAESI Act; 75% deposit condition for appeal was read down to 'may be required' not mandatory
Secured creditors' priority over unsecured in liquidation; SARFAESI enforcement survives liquidation
IBC moratorium prevents SARFAESI action once CIRP begins; automatic stay on proceedings
Swiss Ribbons Pvt Ltd v. Union of India
Upheld IBC's constitutionality; distinction between financial creditors and operational creditors is valid; resolution over liquidation is objective
Committee of Creditors of Essar Steel v. Satish Kumar Gupta
CoC's commercial wisdom supreme in approval of resolution plan; courts cannot interfere with commercial decisions; NCLTs must not micromanage
Vijay Kumar Ghai v. State of West Bengal
Bank employee is public servant under IPC for purpose of bribery offences; Prevention of Corruption Act applies
Vinod Kumar Aggarwal v. Directorate of Enforcement
ED can attach property of guarantor under PMLA even without making guarantor accused
Reaffirmed Shankari Prasad; Parliament can amend all parts of Constitution
Parliament cannot amend FRs (prospective overruling); overruled by Kesavananda
Basic Structure Doctrine: Parliament can amend Constitution but cannot destroy its basic structure; landmark 13-judge bench
Art.21: 'procedure established by law' must be fair, just, reasonable; expanded personal liberty; connected Art.14, 19, 21
Balance between FRs and DPSPs is basic structure; 42nd Amendment provisions giving primacy to DPSPs over FRs struck down
Imposition of President's Rule under Art.356 is subject to judicial review; floor test to determine majority
Guidelines on sexual harassment at workplace; subsequently codified in POSH Act 2013
Union of India v. Association for Democratic Reforms
Right to know about candidates in elections is part of Art.19(1)(a); disclosure of criminal antecedents, assets mandatory
Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
Section 377 IPC decriminalised for consensual acts between adults; unanimous 5-judge bench
Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (Aadhaar)
Privacy is fundamental right under Art.21 (9-judge bench); Aadhaar upheld for government benefits; not mandatory for private entities

cells: Codifies right to privacy; consent-based data processing; Data Fiduciary obligations; Data Principals' rights; significant financial penalties up to Rs.250 crore
Statutory basis for mediation; Pre-litigation mediation; mediator registration; confidentiality; enforceability of mediated settlement agreements
Automatic stay on challenged awards (2019); 2021 restored position of no automatic stay; 8th Schedule qualifications for arbitrators
Fast-track courts for commercial disputes; mandatory pre-institution mediation; costs awarded more liberally
Decriminalises minor offences across 42 Central Acts; fines in place of imprisonment; reduces compliance burden on businesses
33% seats in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies reserved for women; effective after delimitation (post 2026 Census)
NRI Marriage Amendment to Hindu Marriage Act
NRI spouses who desert within 6 months of marriage can have their passport revoked and can be tried in absentia
